name: Dark Heliotrope Grey
lede: Dark Heliotrope Grey is a dim, purplish grey, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[heliotrope-grey]], traced to Ridgway's 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A darkened heliotrope grey
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[heliotrope-grey]], itself named for the pale purple of the heliotrope flower, muted toward grey [1]. The library dates the swatch to Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate L, and again places it in the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, in the block for purplish gray [1]. Ridgway's plates survive only as scans of an aged, printed chart, so the hex value is an approximation of the original ink, not a measurement of it [1].

The closest named neighbors on file are [[purple-slate]] and [[purple-slate]], both almost indistinguishable from it [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 288 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.21 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is rare before 1800, then rises through the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, peaking in a small sample of 1940s paintings [2]. Danish painters Peter Hansen, Niels Larsen Stevns and Theodor Philipsen all have it well above the archive's average rate [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
